did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ecclesiastes calls people to remember their Creator in the days of their youth, before the days of old age come, when they may say they have no delight in them.
Did you know? The description of old age begins with images of the sun, light, moon, and stars being darkened, and of clouds returning after the rain.

Did you know? Ecclesiastes describes the weakening of the body through images of the guardians of the house trembling, the strong men stooping, the grinders becoming few, and those who look through the windows growing dim.
Did you know? The passage also describes doors being shut, the sound of the mill growing faint, waking at the sound of a bird, and the weakening of the voice and singing.

Did you know? Ecclesiastes portrays old age as a time when people fear heights and obstacles along the way, and concludes with a description of their going to their eternal home while mourners circle the streets.
Did you know? Death is described through four images: the silver cord being severed, the golden bowl breaking, the pitcher shattering at the spring, and the wheel running into the pit.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes distinguishes between the body, which returns to the dust as it was, and the spirit, which returns to God who gave it.
Did you know? The phrase “vanity of vanities” appears again here as Ecclesiastes’ conclusion: “Everything is vanity.”
Did you know? Ecclesiastes did not keep his wisdom to himself: he taught the people, listened, investigated, and arranged many proverbs.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes sought to find words of delight, but he also emphasized the need for integrity and truthful words.
Did you know? The words of the wise are compared to goads and firmly embedded nails, and are described as being given by one Shepherd.
Did you know? Ecclesiastes warns against making many books without end and against excessive study, which can weary the body.
Did you know? The practical conclusion of the book is to fear God and keep his commandments, because this is “the whole duty of humanity.”
Did you know? Ecclesiastes teaches that every deed will be brought into judgment, including hidden acts, whether good or evil.
